text: I am Dr. Agent. You are here for hematuria and right flank pain; to start, are you experiencing fever, nausea, or visible blood clots in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma. The combination of hematuria, right flank pain, a history of recurrent UTIs, and the patient's age makes malignancy the primary concern over simple infection or stones. I will now request imaging to confirm this. REQUEST IMAGES: Right abdominal CT with contrast.
